title: Smallness of modules with prescribed local models on a small ringed site
statement: Fix a Grothendieck universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with finite limits and terminal object $1$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings whose section sets belong to $\mathcal V$. Module sheaves have section sets in $\mathcal V$ and mean the sectionwise modules of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, fix a $\mathcal V$-small set $I_U$ and a family $(B_{U,t})_{t\in I_U}$ of module sheaves over $R|_U$ on the slice site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of $R$-module sheaves $M$ for which there is a covering family $\{U_j\to1\}_j$ and indices $t_j\in I_{U_j}$ with $M|_{U_j}\cong B_{U_j,t_j}$. Then $\mathcal P$ is $\mathcal V$-essentially small: there is a set $S\in\mathcal V$ and a family $(M_s)_{s\in S}$ of members of $\mathcal P$ such that every member of $\mathcal P$ is isomorphic to some $M_s$. No Noetherian, scheme, finite-generation or effectivity-of-arbitrary-descent-data hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps (unique gluing of maps), with the small-site local-model counting argument of literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-six-functors-basics/sk-lem-brown-hypotheses/sk-lem-brown-hypotheses-small.proof.md, Essentially small paragraph

proof.text: For any object $W$ and two fixed module sheaves $A,B$ on $\mathcal C/W$ with section sets in $\mathcal V$, a module morphism is determined by its component functions. Thus its Hom set embeds into $\prod_{(T\to W)\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C/W)}\operatorname{Map}(A(T\to W),B(T\to W))$. The slice has a $\mathcal V$-small object set, since its objects are arrows of $\mathcal C$ ending at $W$. Every factor is in $\mathcal V$; naturality and linearity merely specify a subset of this product. In particular both this Hom set and its subset of isomorphisms belong to $\mathcal V$. This is direct counting of natural transformations, not essential smallness of all module sheaves.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph; explicit small-site local-model counting argument

proof.text: Choose once and for all products $W_{UV}=U\times_1 V$, with their two projections, for all objects $U,V$. For $K\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $t\in\prod_{U\in K}I_U$, put $B_U=B_{U,t_U}$ and form the set of families $g_{UV}:B_U|_{W_{UV}}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_V|_{W_{UV}}$ indexed by $K\times K$. Restrictions here are along the respective projections to $U$ and $V$. Each isomorphism set is small by step 1. Let $D$ consist of all triples $(K,t,(g_{UV}))$, without imposing a cover or cocycle condition. Then $D\in\mathcal V$: its construction uses the power set of the small object set, small products of the $I_U$ and isomorphism sets, and small indexed unions. Including unrealizable data only enlarges the small indexing set.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph; explicit small-site local-model counting argument

proof.text: Every $M\in\mathcal P$ realizes a code in $D$. Start with a witnessing cover $\{U_j\to1\}_j$. Let $K$ be its object support, a subset of $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$. For each $U\in K$, choose one occurrence in that cover and retain its label $t_U$ and trivialization $a_U:M|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}B_U$. Define $g_{UV}=(a_V|_{W_{UV}})(a_U|_{W_{UV}})^{-1}$. Both sources are $M|_{W_{UV}}$ by the sectionwise restriction rule. Thus these maps give a member of $D$. In what follows the original covering family is retained, using $a_{U_j}$ on every occurrence, including repeated ones. There is no assertion that deletion of repeated cover members remains a covering in the original coverage.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph; explicit small-site local-model counting argument

proof.text: Suppose $M,N$ realize the same code $d=(K,t,g)$, with trivializations $a_U:M|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}B_U$ and $b_U:N|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}B_U$, and witnessing covers with object support $K$. Set $h_U=b_U^{-1}a_U$. On $W_{UV}$ the common-code identities give $a_V=g_{UV}a_U$ and $b_V=g_{UV}b_U$, so $b_V^{-1}a_V=(g_{UV}b_U)^{-1}(g_{UV}a_U)=b_U^{-1}a_U$. These are equalities of restricted module morphisms on the whole overlap slice. The inverse maps $h_U^{-1}=a_U^{-1}b_U$ agree there too, by taking inverses of this equality. Use the witnessing cover for $M$ for both families; every one of its objects lies in $K$, where both trivializations are available.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph; explicit small-site local-model counting argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] to this original cover of $1$, first to $(h_{U_j})_j$ and then to $(h_{U_j}^{-1})_j$. The finite-limit hypothesis supplies every required overlap and pulled-back cover. The lemma gives module morphisms $h:M\to N$ and $k:N\to M$: restriction to $\mathcal C/1$ is the original sheaf, since every object has a unique arrow to $1$. The restrictions of $kh$ and $hk$ to all cover members are identities. The uniqueness assertion of that same lemma gives $kh=\mathrm{id}_M$ and $hk=\mathrm{id}_N$. Hence two realizations of one code are isomorphic. This uses only the morphism-gluing assertion of Stacks Tag 04TQ and its module version, Tag 03EM, not existence of a sheaf for arbitrary descent data.

source.place: Tag 03EM, lemma-internal-hom, using sites.tex Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; apply to the maps and their inverses

proof.text: Let $S\subseteq D$ be the subset of codes realized by members of $\mathcal P$; then $S\in\mathcal V$. Choose one realizing $M_s\in\mathcal P$ for each $s\in S$. This is ordinary set-indexed choice: in an ambient universe containing $\mathcal V$, all the $\mathcal V$-valued module sheaves on the fixed small category form a set (each sheaf's section sets, operations and restriction graphs together are coded in $\mathcal V$). Thus this choice does not require choice from proper classes. For any $M\in\mathcal P$, step 3 gives a realized code $s$, and steps 4–5 identify $M\cong M_s$. The required indexing set is $S\in\mathcal V$, regardless of the auxiliary ambient universe used to describe the choice. If $S$ is empty, the empty family suffices.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q60-ec74d7703 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Ordinary first split (0 new nodes, statement and stmt_deps unchanged) of a statement-only node that Q67 created on 2026-10-21 when re-splitting det-brown-hypotheses-small. This item has no repair note of its own. It is not superseded: live and side-live still show it unsplit. No SGA is cited. The statement is true and its proof is complete. Step 1: Hom sets inject into a product over the small slice of maps between V-valued section sets. Step 2: the codes (K ⊆ Ob C, labels, isomorphisms g_UV on fixed products U×V) form a set in V, built from a power set, small products and unions, with no cocycle condition. Step 3: each M has a code; one occurrence is chosen per object and the original indexed cover is kept, so no repetition deletion is assumed (consistent with the reindexing-only site convention). Step 4: a_V=g a_U and b_V=g b_U give b_V^{-1}a_V=b_U^{-1}a_U; I checked the order of composition, and the self-overlap U×U is covered by g_UU. Step 5: lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing (Stacks 03EM via 04TQ, sites.tex l.5637 read) glues the maps and their inverses on C/1=C, and its uniqueness gives inverse isomorphisms. Its hypotheses hold: R is commutative, finite limits give the overlaps, the cover is of 1. Step 6: representatives are chosen for the realized codes S ∈ V. Edge cases checked: empty I_U, an empty cover of 1 (modules are 0), singleton cover, repeated members, non-monic cover arrows. rg found no duplicate in the DAG. The gluing nodes for open covers and for étale sites are specialisations. Tool_use lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing is accepted as a generic off-unit black box.
